channel.title: Morningstar News
channel.description: UK news, Pokemon, Warhammer, Star Trek, AI, Android, macOS, Linux. Published daily.

item.title: Pensions and benefits go dark as the DWP battles a cyber incident
item.description: Saturday's paper: a department offline, a discounter on the block, and the mathematicians quietly worrying about their padlocks.

item.title: Ninety-Two Labour MPs Tell Burnham: Not Rosebank
item.description: A party split over oil, migration at its lowest since 1997, and a Midlands road scheme quietly binned to pay for defence.

item.title: The dinghy salesman at the centre of the Channel crossings
item.description: A German boat dealer named in the smuggling files, two Brexit treaties with a ten-year handbrake, and Gordon Ramsay handed the keys to Top Gear

item.title: Energy bills to jump 26% in January, and the Met is told it still hasn't changed
item.description: A brutal price cap, a damning police review, and Derby's hospitals declaring themselves overwhelmed

item.title: Nvidia's board puts Jensen Huang back in the chair
item.description: A returning chief executive, a benefits review that wants to rehumanise Pip, and the BBC's Christmas line-up

item.title: Tear gas, or something like it, empties a Manchester arena
item.description: A major incident at Co-op Live, the NHS hands 700,000 mammograms to a machine, and Star Trek's best film turns thirty

item.title: The data watchdog lifts its own gagging orders
item.description: Miliband unties Brussels from tuition fees, a regulator apologises to its own staff, and Star Trek discovers it has been living in Apple's shop all along.

item.title: Burnham comes back from Brussels with a deal, and the Brexit argument restarts
item.description: Britain signs a post-Brexit reset in Brussels, a rape case reopens the consent debate, and a cancer pill does something genuinely startling in a trial.

item.title: Ground Rent, Meet the Peppercorn
item.description: Leasehold is to be abolished in all but name, the Bayesian inquiry finds a risk nobody had assessed, and Anthropic goes public at a number that stops conversation.

item.title: Petrol Pushes Inflation Back Up, and Nobody Wants to Say the Word
item.description: A 12-month high in the cost of living, a river you cannot swim in, and a great many websites quietly serving malware through a tool they all trusted.

item.title: Complete Reset, With a Bill Attached
item.description: Milburn's review lands in full, snow on the Peak District, and Google breaks its own cameras.

item.title: Britain's Youth Jobs Plan Arrives With a Bill Attached
item.description: Milburn's verdict lands tomorrow, the NHS revolts over zero-hours, and an AI can now pay for things.

item.title: Google shipped its November update a month early and broke the lock screen
item.description: Pixel QPR2 arrives ahead of schedule with 33 fixes and a few new problems, Children in Need tops £38m, and the Orks get a codex.
